questions.question: Who is Jeff?
questions.answer: Jeff is a Domestic Shorthair cat who lives in southern New Hampshire.
questions.comment: That's me!

questions.question: Can I meet Jeff?
questions.answer: If you're reading this, that means you've already met Jeff. I'm sure he's happy that you're here!

questions.question: Okay, but can I actually meet Jeff?
questions.answer: No, sorry. Jeff is shy, lives indoors, and is not currently accepting visitors, interviews, or requests for his autograph.
questions.comment: Stranger danger!

questions.question: Is "Jefferson" his real name?
questions.answer: Yes, Jefferson Elmer is his real government name. He arrived with the name "Jefferson" and, when questioned about it, gives us a narrowed gaze and refuses to answer.
questions.comment: I'm a cat. What were you expecting, a birth certificate?

questions.question: Why is his middle name Elmer?
questions.answer:
I gave him that name because he looks like he was assembled with glue. I assure you, however, that Jeff is structurally sound.

...mostly.

questions.question: How old is Jeff?
questions.answer: The shelter estimates that Jeff was born around 2018. So, about 8 years old.
questions.comment: I expect birthday presents every year. The humans have yet to disappoint me.

questions.question: Why does Jeff look different in every picture?
questions.answer: These photos were taken with different cameras, settings, lighting, and angles. We also believe that there is a possibility of Jeff using similar-looking cats as stand-ins for public appearances.
questions.comment: They often take my picture without permission, so I'm not always photo-ready. It's pretty rude, really.

questions.question: Did Jeff approve these pictures?
questions.answer: Jeff was given several opportunities to comment. He responded by flopping onto his back and rolling around for a moment or two.

questions.question: Where does Jeff like to nap?
questions.answer: Everywhere.
questions.comment: Everywhere.

questions.question: What does Jeff do when nobody is watching?
questions.answer: We're not sure. At night, we hear him meowing and playing with his toys. So probably just that.
questions.comment: I have a pretty elusive life out of the limelight. None of you need to know about it. I like it that way.

questions.question: Is this entire website really dedicated to... a cat?
questions.answer: Yeah. It is.
questions.comment: I've been told that cats practically run the internet. Are you surprised?

questions.question: Are you tracking me?
questions.answer: I monitor how many times particular pages are visited and interacted with. Besides that? Nope.
questions.comment: I've been following your scent since you got here. Do you have any treats?

questions.question: Why are there exactly 150 pictures?
questions.answer:
Originally, there were only 100. But they didn't quite capture the full range of Jeff's personality.

200 would have been too overwhelming to discover all of, but there are even more than that in my personal Jeff trove.
questions.comment: 151 of them would just be silly. Who would collect 151 of something?

questions.question: Will more pictures be added later?
questions.answer:
Probably not. The website has limited storage, and Jeff's complete photographic archive could threaten the structural integrity of this webpage. A webpage which is loosely held together with masking tape, magic, and cat hair.

...a LOT of cat hair.
questions.comment: I have a strict licensing agreement that was set up by my lawyers. The humans need to abide by it.

questions.question: Why did I see the same picture again?
questions.answer:
Jeff believes that every photograph of him demands an encore.

The website does avoid repeating pictures that have been displayed recently, but previously discovered ones will eventually return.
questions.comment: You're welcome.

questions.question: Where is my progress saved?
questions.answer: Your discoveries and settings are stored locally in your browser. Clearing your browser data or using a different browser gives Jeff the opportunity to pretend that you have never met him.

questions.question: What does the NEW! message mean?
questions.answer: That means you've uncovered a new picture! It will be added into your gallery.
questions.comment: The last few pictures may be tough to uncover. Don't worry if you don't see them right away, I'll be sure to push them your way if you stick around long enough.

questions.question: Why are some pages "LOCKED" behind viewing pictures of Jeff?
questions.answer: Jeff can be pretty shy, and needs to get to know you before he's willing to open up to you. Don't take it too personally.
questions.comment: If you get too close without my permission, I'll exercise my right to fight-or-flight.

questions.question: Is there a deeper meaning or secret to this website?
questions.answer: No, not really. I just made this website so everybody can get the chance to... you know. "Meet Jeff."
questions.comment: meOwMEOWmEOWMeoWmEOwmEoWmEOWmeOW? Listen closely to my V01CE.

questions.question: What happens when I find all 150 pictures?
questions.answer: You don't expect me to spoil the ending, do you?

categories.label: The Humans
categories.subtitle: Questions about the humans behind the page

questions.question: What can you tell us about Jeff's humans?
questions.answer: Jeff lives in a home with three humans. One is my mother, the second is my brother, and the third is my grandmother. Each time I come to visit, I try to take a new picture of Jeff. This website is a compilation of many of these photos.
questions.comment: They feed me, and give me the attention I deserve. What else do you really need to know?

questions.question: Who takes Jeff's pictures?
questions.answer: I've taken most of these photos. A few were sourced from family.

questions.question: Why aren't Jeff's humans featured in his images?
questions.answer: We don't think that Jeff is ready to share the spotlight. Besides, this website is dedicated to Jeff, not us!
questions.comment: And yet you call ME shy...

questions.question: Who made this website?
questions.answer: Me!
questions.comment: Him!

questions.question: Did you tell Jeff about this website?
questions.answer: Yes, he has been informed. When I disclosed the project to him, he stared at me for several seconds and then left the room.
questions.comment: I can neither confirm nor deny my approval of this violation of my privacy.

questions.question: Why are there "Meet Jeff" stickers?
questions.answer: Stickers were given to friends and family with instructions to place them alongside other stickers in designated public art spaces. If you found a sticker and arrived here, then the Jeff experiment has succeeded.

questions.question: This sticker shouldn't be here. How can I remove it?
questions.answer: Whoops... sorry about that. Carefully lift a corner with your fingernail or a plastic edge and peel slowly. If appropriate for the surface, gentle heat may help loosen the adhesive. If residue remains, use a surface-appropriate adhesive remover or isopropyl alcohol only after testing it in an inconspicuous area.
questions.comment: Pesky vandals.
